reviews.summary: The lead was still about the funny ones and gave no classic message; 'the one line that isn't' needed rereading; 'print and cut the slips' didn't say how, though two of the top ten are printables.

Every template claim matches schema.ts and Template.tsx, down to the sparkle cookie that can be opened first, and the Spanish reads like Spain; the sample lines are original and deadpan where the top results recycle the same lists.

Answers all four People-also-ask questions and explains how to write a fortune, which no top result does, but says nothing about where fortune cookies come from (result 9 and a PAA cover it) and gives no slip size for the printable searchers.

applied: Lead now opens with what a fortune cookie message is and a real classic line, in both languages
Love section lead-in reworded ('the one serious line on a plate of jokes')
Slip size and font for homemade cookies (about 6 by 1.5 cm, 2¼ by ½ inches)

One sentence on where fortune cookies come from (Japanese-run bakeries in California, spread through US Chinese restaurants after the Second World War, rare in China) and that the classic list suits a children's party or classroom

Polish: 'Most real fortunes', H2 'Classic fortune cookie messages and quotes', two classic lines changed to avoid echoing the door and phone jokes, 'Alguien misterioso' instead of 'Una desconocida misteriosa'
rejected: Spanish title 'graciosas, de amor y clásicas' (polish): 65 characters, over the 60 the test allows

reviews.summary: All three fixes made. Lists stop at 'here are 100 quotes'; this post gives classic, funny and love fortunes, the shapes behind them, a method for in-jokes, meaningful lucky numbers and three ways to get slips into cookies tonight.
The new passages are right, but the slip size's two units disagree: 1.5 cm is about 5/8 inch, not 1/2.

Both fixes made. It is the only first-page result that shows how to write a funny or tender fortune for one person, and it still has the classic and funny lists, love lines, all four People-also-ask answers, the history and the slip size.

applied: Slip size now 2¼ by ⅝ inches to match 6 by 1.5 cm
Polish: Spanish 'a cualquiera que abra la galleta' (no antecedent for 'la'); full stops after closing guillemets in the Spanish lead and first FAQ answer
rejected: Naming Yasuko Nakamachi as the historian (polish): the claim stands as written and a name adds nothing the reader acts on
Reader polish (font point size, first takeaway, a 'real' bought fortune in the lead) and search polish (a printable sheet): optional, kept out to avoid unreviewed new text

reviews.summary: The top results are shops or numbered lists of pasted fortunes; this one gives classic, funny and love lines plus the method behind them, so you can write a plate of fortunes for one particular person tonight.

The slip-size fix is right (1.5 cm is about 5/8 inch), every template claim matches schema.ts and Template.tsx, and the Spanish reads like Spain; the origin note is the established account with nothing invented.

Original lines, the four-shapes table, personalisable lines, the in-joke method, meaningful lucky numbers and practical slip advice beat the shops, printable dumps and 40-to-100-line listicles, and all four People-also-ask questions are answered.

Reader: 2⅜ instead of 2¼ inches, a point size for the font
Search: a printable sheet of the lines at slip size
